page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor with 16 vCPUs, 8 physical cores, and a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Graphics processing is handled by a single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 225 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance offers a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between CPU-only workloads and GPU-accelerated tasks. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 25% tier, while multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth consistently rank in the middle 50%. Conversely, the hardware excels at machine learning tasks; LLM inference speed for prompt processing using small (135M) and medium (7B) models ranks in the top 10% tier, with text generation speeds for these models placing in the top 25%. Prompt processing for large (70B) models falls back to the middle 50% tier.

Given the hardware profile, this instance offers a specialized resource density where the inclusion of a dedicated NVIDIA T4 GPU offsets the lower single-core CPU performance. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that can offload computation to the GPU rather than relying solely on raw CPU clock speeds. Appropriate workloads include graphics-intensive applications, machine learning inference (specifically small to medium LLMs), and GPU-accelerated database operations, whereas CPU-bound single-threaded tasks represent a performance tradeoff.

The hardware includes a dedicated NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, a 225 GB NVMe SSD, and 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.
